    x, y, d = q.popleft()

title: Shortest Route
statement: A country has n cities and m two-way roads, each with a positive length. Find the length of the shortest route from city 1 to city n, or report that there is none.
input_format: Line 1: two integers n and m. Then m lines, each with three integers u v w (a road between cities u and v of length w).

reference_solution:
import heapq
n, m = map(int, input().split())
adj = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
for _ in range(m):
    u, v, w = map(int, input().split())
    adj[u].append((v, w))
    adj[v].append((u, w))
INF = float("inf")
dist = [INF] * (n + 1)
dist[1] = 0
pq = [(0, 1)]
while pq:
    d, u = heapq.heappop(pq)
    if d > dist[u]:
        continue
    for v, w in adj[u]:
        if d + w < dist[v]:
            dist[v] = d + w
            heapq.heappush(pq, (dist[v], v))
print(-1 if dist[n] == INF else dist[n])

title: Sliding Window Maximum
statement: A window of size w slides one position at a time from the left end of an array to the right end. Report the maximum value inside the window at every position.
input_format: Line 1: two integers n and w. Line 2: n space separated integers.
output_format: Print the n - w + 1 window maximums on one line, separated by single spaces.
sample_explanations: The windows are [1,3,-1], [3,-1,-3], ... with maximums 3 3 5 5 6 7.
One window covers everything and its maximum is 9.
reference_solution:
from collections import deque
n, w = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
dq = deque()
out = []
for i, x in enumerate(a):
    while dq and a[dq[-1]] <= x:
        dq.pop()
    dq.append(i)
    if dq[0] <= i - w:
        dq.popleft()
    if i >= w - 1:
        out.append(a[dq[0]])
print(" ".join(map(str, out)))

title: Largest Rectangle in a Histogram
statement: A histogram has n bars of width 1 and the given heights. Find the area of the largest rectangle that fits entirely inside the histogram, with its base on the bottom line.
input_format: Line 1: an integer n. Line 2: n space separated non-negative integers (bar heights).
output_format: Print the largest rectangle area.
sample_explanations: The bars of heights 5 and 6 form a rectangle of width 2 and height 5: area 10.
Either the bar of 4 alone (area 4) or both bars at height 2 (area 4).
reference_solution:
n = int(input())
h = list(map(int, input().split())) + [0]
st = []
best = 0
for i, x in enumerate(h):
    while st and h[st[-1]] >= x:
        top = st.pop()
        width = i if not st else i - st[-1] - 1
        best = max(best, h[top] * width)
    st.append(i)
print(best)

        low = min(low, h[j])
        best = max(best, low * (j - i + 1))

title: Knapsack Best Value
statement: You have a bag that holds at most W units of weight and a set of items, each with a weight and a value. Choose some of the items (each at most once) so that the total weight does not exceed W and the total value is as large as possible.
input_format: Line 1: two integers n and W. Then n lines, each with the weight and the value of an item.
output_format: Print the maximum total value.
sample_explanations: Taking the items of weight 20 and 30 gives value 220 within the limit.
Neither item fits in the bag, so the value is 0.
reference_solution:
n, W = map(int, input().split())
items = [tuple(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]
dp = [0] * (W + 1)
for w, v in items:
    for c in range(W, w - 1, -1):
        dp[c] = max(dp[c], dp[c - w] + v)
print(dp[W])
